full_judgment:
Mr. Muhammad Ansar Ali, J :- This rule arises out of an application u/s 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by accused petitioner Moslemuddin Sheikh in a pending case being G. R. Case No. 19 of 1991 arising out of Shibalay P. S. Case No. 10 (3) 91 under section 395/397 of the Penal Code. 

 2. The case of the prosecution as made out in the F. I. R. in short is that on 4.3.91 at about 9.30 P.M. the complainant who is a shareng started his motor launch from Arichaghat for Doulatdiaghat with passengers but after about 20/22 minutes he heard cries inside the launch and then 7/8 dacoits gheraoed him with deadly weapons and asked him to change the direction of the launch and forced him to take the launch to the chaf on the western side of the River Jamuna. Thereafter the dacoits attacked the passengers and looted away their cash money and various other articles and then left the launch and fled away. The complainant thereafter came back with his launch to Arichaghat and lodged the F.I.R. with the Shibalay P.S. on 20.3.1991 in respect of the above occurrence but without any name of any accused. The Police started investigation of the case and arrested this petitioner on suspicion and then produced him before a Magistrate who recorded this alleged confession on 25.3.91 and then the accused was sent to jail-custody. The police on conclusion of the investigation, submitted charge sheet under Section 395/397 of the Penal Code on 15.6.91 against the petitioner and some others. The petitioner thereafter moved a number of applications for bail on different occasions, but the prayers for bail were rejected by the Upazila now Thana Magistrate. Lastly, he moved an application before the learned Sessions Judge, Manikganj praying for bail and the said application for bail in Misc. Case No. 98 of 1993 after hearing was rejected by the learned Sessions Judge on 7.8.93 mainly for the reason that the accused being arrested on 23.3.91 made a confessional statement before the Magistrate involving himself and others in the case. The petitioner having failed to obtain bail from the court of the learned Sessions Judge, moved this application u/s 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in this Court and obtained the present rule on 11.1.1994. 

 3. Mr. Mir Kashem Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for accused petitioner submits that the petitioner is an innocent tailor who was working at the Abha Sangsta Bazar, Savar and he was arrested by the Police only on suspicion and there-after mercilessly beaten and tortured by the police who forced him to make a so-called confession before the Magistrate which was subsequently retracted by the petitioner as false and involuntary. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the petitioner was not named in the F. I. R, which was lodged after 16 days of the occurrence and further submits that since the arrest of the petitioner on 21.3.91 he is being rotten in the jail-hajat for more than 3 years without any trial of the case which is still pending in the court of the learned Magistrate and there is no sign of any early hearing of the case in the appropriate court, though the charge-sheet was submitted on 15.6.91 about 3 years back. He further submits that the petitioner is the only earning member of his family consisting of 7 members and his old mother is a serious patient of cancer who requires his personal care and attendance and also proper treatment. 

 4. The learned Advocate for the petitioner then refers to the recent amendment of the Code of Criminal Procedure by Act 41 of 1992 and submits that if the trial of an accused cannot be concluded within 360 days, in such circumstances in view of the amended sub-section 4 of Section 339(C) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, he will be entitled to get bail. The learned Advocate pointedly submits and there has been undue, unjustified and unreasonable delay in this case in holding the trial to the serious prejudice and harassment of the petitioner. The case has not been fixed as yet for trial by the proper court due to procrastination and negligence of the prosecution and continuation of this protracted preceding is nothing but an abuse of the process of the court. Hence, the petitioner should be enlarged on bail. The learned Advocate in support of his contentions, relied on a decision in the case of Reasat All Vs. Gholam Muhammad and State reported in 20 DLR (SC) 339, wherein it has been observed that undue or inordinate delay in holding the trial entitles the accused to get the benefit of the privilege of bail even in case of murder. To show similar view he has also referred to a decision in the case of Ahrar Muhammad and others Vs. The State reported in PLD 1974 (SC) 224. 

 5. Mr. S.B. Barua, the learned Advocate appearing for the State, in the facts and circumstances of the case and the undue and unusual delay being caused in holding the trial of the instant case and also in view of the amendment of the Code of Criminal Procedure in sub-section 4 of Section 339(C) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, could not however seriously oppose the prayer of bail of the petitioner. 

 6. We have heard the learned Advocates for both the sides, perused the application and the connected papers including the paradise reply from the state and the decisions cited above, we are of the view that unreasonable or inordinate delay in the trial of a case can be a good ground for granting bail to the accused in the facts and circumstances of each particular case. It may be remembered that speedy trial is the expectation by both the prosecution as well as the defence. And for this, apart from the general principles there has been also specific article in the Constitution of our country. Now, it is further submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that due to procrastination and negligence of the prosecution, this unreasonable delay is being caused in the trial of the petitioner causing him serious prejudice and harassment for no fault of his own. In the instant case, it may be noted that the alleged occurrence took place on 4.3.91. The F.I.R. was lodged on 20.3.91 after about 16 days of the occurrence and this petitioner was arrested on 23.3.91 and thereafter charge-sheet in the case was submitted on 15.6.91 but still now the case has not been transmitted to the proper court for trial and the case is yet pending before the Upazila i.e. Thana Magistrate, Shibalay. It further appears that a parawise reply to the application for bail has been given on behalf of the State but in that nothing has been stated as to the cause of the delay in holding the trial of this case. However, it may be observed that bail cannot be with- held from an accused by way of punishment. Thus having considered the facts and circum-stances of the case and the undue and unreasonable delay in holding the trial of the case, we are inclined to grant bail to the petitioner pending hearing of the case of the ends of justice. 

 7. In the result, we allow this application for bail and make the Rule absolute and direct that the accused petitioner Mosleuddin Shaikh be enlarged on bail to the satisfaction of the Deputy Commissioner, Manikgonj pending hearing of G.R. Case No. 19 of 1991 u/s 395/397 arising out of Shibalay P.S. Case No. 10(3) 91. If there is any abuse or misuse of the privilege of this bail, the trial court will be free to cancel the bail of the petitioner.
